subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should OpenClaw implement incremental append-aware session-memory indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema, and what correctness boundary should it use for overlap, compaction, and source-wide batching?
rationale: The source-level performance problem is real, but the prior offset/hash proposals and open candidate PR do not settle the session-state correctness contract after the memory schema and batching refactors.

options.title: Sponsor a current-schema design
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a replacement implementation against `memory_index_sources` and `memory_index_chunks` with overlap, compaction, batching, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers decide the current full rewrite is the intended correctness tradeoff for session memory.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a current-schema design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a replacement implementation against `memory_index_sources` and `memory_index_chunks` with overlap, compaction, batching, and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history ties jalehman to the session corpus and memory-index identity paths most directly affected by the design choice.
